title: Ridgeline Pro Credit Billing Standard — Start Day of the Interim Payoff Accrual
content:
The interim payoff accrual on a Ridgeline Pro Credit commercial account runs over the accrued days, which end on the payment date. The day the accrual starts is set by the latest closed statement's delinquency and the account's age:

1. When the latest statement shows no more than **30** days past due and the account has been open at least **60** whole months, accrual starts once the tier's late charge grace days after the statement date have passed: the accrued days are the days from the statement date to the payment date less the tier's grace days.
2. When the latest statement shows no more than **30** days past due and the account has been open less than **60** whole months, accrual starts on the day after the statement date: the accrued days are the days from the statement date to the payment date less one.
3. When the latest statement shows more than **30** days past due, accrual starts on the statement date: the accrued days are the days from the statement date to the payment date.

In every case the accrued days are never below zero.

## Conventions

- Days are calendar days, the statement date being day 0.
- Account age is counted in whole calendar months from the account's opening date to the payment date.
- The tier's late charge grace days: Commercial Account Net 30, 0; Net 30 Select, 5; Net 45, 5; Net 60 Enterprise, 10 (the revolving tiers, 0).

## Worked cases (hypothetical: payment 18 days after the statement date, Commercial Account Net 60 Enterprise)

| Days past due on the statement | Account age | Accrued days |
|---|---|---|
| 30 | 75 whole months | 18 less 10, so 8 |
| 30 | 41 whole months | 18 less 1, so 17 |
| 31 | 75 whole months | 18 |
| 12 | 80 whole months, payment 7 days after the statement date | 7 less 10 is below zero, so 0 |
